target.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits to requestTimeoutMs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Codex app-server over websocket/unix transport would hang forever on initialize/RPC when a peer accepted the socket but never completed the WebSocket upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bound upgrades with `ws.handshakeTimeout` **and** an explicit CONNECTING deadline at the transport chokepoint (`createWebSocketTransport`). `ws.handshakeTimeout` alone does **not** abort custom `createConnection` (Unix) upgrades - verified with a never-upgrade peer that stayed CONNECTING past the library timeout.

Production budget is resolved `appServer.requestTimeoutMs` (default 60s) from `CodexAppServerClient.start` via `resolveCodexAppServerRuntimeOptions()`.

**Narrowed to Codex-only (Maintainer option 1, recommended):** Removed the unrelated APNs CodeQL allowlist (`#109357`) and docs-sync typings export (`#109364`) that prior heads bundled to unblock CI. Those are main pre-existing debt and should land independently. This branch now touches only Codex runtime, Codex tests, and the Codex harness doc.

Documented the expanded `requestTimeoutMs` contract in `docs/plugins/codex-harness.md` so operators know it also bounds WebSocket/Unix upgrade handshakes.

Collision check: [#108795](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108795) closed unmerged; APNs allowlist split [#109357](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109357); typings unblocker [#109364](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109364).

## User Impact

- **Before:** never-upgrade peers hang initialize/RPC forever (TCP and Unix).
- **After:** handshake follows operator `requestTimeoutMs` (default 60s) on both TCP and Unix, then emits transport exit (`1006`).

## Verification

- Exact head: `d002f8ef49e59db3e726c33585e35882ffeec50c`
- `oxfmt --check` (4 files) - passed; exit 0.
- `oxlint` (3 TS files) - passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` - passed; exit 0.

Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts > Codex app-server websocket transport > can speak JSON-RPC over websocket transport 73ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts > Codex app-server websocket transport > can speak JSON-RPC over the canonical unix control socket 12ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts > Codex app-server websocket transport > negative control: ws without handshakeTimeout stays CONNECTING on never-upgrade peer 308ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts > Codex app-server websocket transport > emits exit when the websocket handshake never completes 204ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts > Codex app-server websocket transport > honors a non-default handshake budget on the TCP transport path 254ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts > Codex app-server websocket transport > honors a non-default handshake budget on the Unix transport path 256ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts > Codex app-server websocket transport > fails initialize when the websocket handshake never completes 206ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

Mutation check: the negative-control test (test 3) proves the bug exists without the fix - `ws` without `handshakeTimeout` stays CONNECTING (`readyState=0`, `outcome=still-pending`) after 300ms. With the fix, tests 4-7 observe bounded exit `1006` within the configured budget.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a never-upgrading Codex app-server peer that accepts the TCP/Unix socket but never sends HTTP Upgrade headers is terminated within the configured `requestTimeoutMs` budget instead of hanging forever.

Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22, real `net.Server` loopback on `127.0.0.1` and real Unix domain sockets, real `ws` WebSocket client (no mocked transport).

Exact commands run:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

Observed output:

```text
[codex handshake negative control] outcome=still-pending readyState=0 wait_ms=300 without_handshakeTimeout=true
[codex handshake proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=201 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=200 production_ms=60000
[codex handshake tcp non-default] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=250 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=250
[codex handshake unix non-default] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=251 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=250
[codex handshake initialize proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=203 message=initialize transport failed after request write: WebSocket was closed before the connection was established
```

Evidence:
- Negative control: without `handshakeTimeout`, WebSocket stays CONNECTING (`readyState=0`) after 300ms wait - bug proven
- TCP path: exits `1006` at 201ms with 200ms budget; production budget is 60s
- Unix path: exits `1006` at 251ms with 250ms budget - `ws.handshakeTimeout` alone does not abort Unix `createConnection`
- Initialize: `initialize` fails with "WebSocket was closed before the connection was established" at 203ms
- All 7 tests pass including 2 pre-existing JSON-RPC transport tests (no regression)

What was not tested: live remote Codex app-server with provider credentials; non-Linux Unix domain socket implementations; `ws` library internals beyond the public `handshakeTimeout` + `terminate` API.

## Risk / Compatibility

Medium (timeout policy). Legitimate upgrades slower than `requestTimeoutMs` now exit `1006`. This reuses an existing operator setting (no new config surface) and the default 60s is generous for handshake-only. The expanded contract is documented in `docs/plugins/codex-harness.md`.

CI note: touching `transport-websocket.ts` triggers the full CodeQL `network-runtime-boundary` scan, which currently fails on main's unclassified `openApnsTlsTunnel` `tls.connect`. That is pre-existing main debt tracked in [#109357](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109357) and should not block this Codex runtime fix.
